items.title: Ensure 'Enforce password history' is set to '24 or more password(s)'
items.source: (net accounts | Select-String 'Length of password history maintained' | Out-String) -replace '[^0-9]',''
items.powershell_check: (net accounts | Select-String 'Length of password history maintained' | Out-String) -replace '[^0-9]',''
items.remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Enforce password history to '24 or more password(s)'
items.reason: The longer a password is reused, the greater the chance that a threat actor can determine the password through brute force attacks. Also, accounts that may have been compromised will remain exploitable if the password is left unchanged. If password changes are required but password reuse is not prevented, or if a continually small number of passwords are reused, the effectiveness of a good password policy is greatly reduced.
guidance: Check the configuration source: (net accounts | Select-String 'Length of password history maintained' | Out-String) -replace '[^0-9]',''
Expected value: 24

Reason: The longer a password is reused, the greater the chance that a threat actor can determine the password through brute force attacks. Also, accounts that may have been compromised will remain exploitable if the password is left unchanged. If password changes are required but password reuse is not prevented, or if a continually small number of passwords are reused, the effectiveness of a good password policy is greatly reduced.
Rule: Ensure 'Enforce password history' is set to '24 or more password(s)'
Remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Enforce password history to '24 or more password(s)'

items.title: Ensure 'Maximum password age' is set to '365 or fewer days, but not 0'
items.remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Maximum password age to '365 or fewer days, but not 0'
items.reason: The longer a password exists the higher the likelihood that it will be compromised by a brute force attack, a threat actor gaining general knowledge about the user, or by the user sharing the password. Configuring the Maximum password age setting to 0 so that users are never required to change their passwords is a major security risk because that allows a compromised password to be used by the threat actor for as long as the valid user has authorized access.

items.title: Ensure 'Minimum password age' is set to '1 or more day(s)'
items.remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Minimum password age to '1 or more day(s)'
items.reason: Users may have favorite passwords that they like to use because they are easy to remember Unfortunately, passwords are compromised and if a threat actor is targeting a specific individual's user account, with foreknowledge of data about that user, reuse of old passwords can cause a security breach. To address password reuse, a combination of security settings is required. Using this policy setting with the Enforce password history setting prevents the easy reuse of old passwords.
guidance: Check the configuration source: (net accounts | Select-String 'Minimum password age' | Out-String) -replace '[^0-9]',''
Expected value: 1

Reason: Users may have favorite passwords that they like to use because they are easy to remember Unfortunately, passwords are compromised and if a threat actor is targeting a specific individual's user account, with foreknowledge of data about that user, reuse of old passwords can cause a security breach. To address password reuse, a combination of security settings is required. Using this policy setting with the Enforce password history setting prevents the easy reuse of old passwords.
Rule: Ensure 'Minimum password age' is set to '1 or more day(s)'
Remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Minimum password age to '1 or more day(s)'

items.title: Ensure 'Minimum password length' is set to '14 or more character(s)'
items.remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Minimum password length to '14 or more character(s)'
items.reason: Types of password attacks include dictionary attacks (which attempt to use common words and phrases) and brute force attacks (which try every possible combination of characters). Also, threat actors sometimes try to obtain the account database so they can use tools to discover the accounts and passwords.
guidance: Check the configuration source: (net accounts | Select-String 'Minimum password length' | Out-String) -replace '[^0-9]',''
Expected value: 14

Reason: Types of password attacks include dictionary attacks (which attempt to use common words and phrases) and brute force attacks (which try every possible combination of characters). Also, threat actors sometimes try to obtain the account database so they can use tools to discover the accounts and passwords.
Rule: Ensure 'Minimum password length' is set to '14 or more character(s)'
Remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Minimum password length to '14 or more character(s)'

items.title: Ensure 'Password must meet complexity requirements' is set to 'Enabled'

items.reason: Passwords that contain only alphanumeric characters are extremely easy to discover with several publicly available tools.
guidance: Check the configuration source: & secedit /export /cfg $env:TEMP\secpol.inf /quiet; if (Test-Path $env:TEMP\secpol.inf) { Select-String -Path $env:TEMP\secpol.inf -Pattern '^PasswordComplexity' | ForEach-Object { ($_ -split '=')[-1].Trim() } }
Expected value: 1
Reason: Passwords that contain only alphanumeric characters are extremely easy to discover with several publicly available tools.
Rule: Ensure 'Password must meet complexity requirements' is set to 'Enabled'
Remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Password must meet complexity requirements to 'Enabled'

items.reason: Enabling this policy setting allows the operating system to store passwords in a weaker format that is much more susceptible to compromise and weakens your system security.

items.title: Ensure 'Account lockout duration' is set to '15 or more minute(s)'
items.remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy\Account lockout duration to '15 or more minute(s)'
items.reason: A denial-of-service (DoS) condition can be created if a threat actor abuses the Account lockout threshold and repeatedly attempts to log on with a specific account. Once the Account lockout threshold setting is configured, the account will be locked out after the specified number of failed attempts. If Account lockout duration is set to 0, then the account will remain locked out until an administrator unlocks it manually.
guidance: Check the configuration source: (net accounts | Select-String 'Lockout duration' | Out-String) -replace '[^0-9]',''
Expected value: 15

Reason: A denial-of-service (DoS) condition can be created if a threat actor abuses the Account lockout threshold and repeatedly attempts to log on with a specific account. Once the Account lockout threshold setting is configured, the account will be locked out after the specified number of failed attempts. If Account lockout duration is set to 0, then the account will remain locked out until an administrator unlocks it manually.
Rule: Ensure 'Account lockout duration' is set to '15 or more minute(s)'
Remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy\Account lockout duration to '15 or more minute(s)'

items.title: Ensure 'Account lockout threshold' is set to '5 or fewer invalid logon attempt(s), but not 0'
items.remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy\Account lockout threshold to '5 or fewer invalid logon attempt(s), but not 0'
items.reason: Setting an account lockout threshold reduces the likelihood that an online password brute force attack will be successful. Setting the account lockout threshold too low introduces risk of increased accidental lockouts and/or a threat actor intentionally locking out accounts.
guidance: Check the configuration source: (net accounts | Select-String 'Lockout threshold' | Out-String) -replace '[^0-9]',''
Expected value: 5

Reason: Setting an account lockout threshold reduces the likelihood that an online password brute force attack will be successful. Setting the account lockout threshold too low introduces risk of increased accidental lockouts and/or a threat actor intentionally locking out accounts.
Rule: Ensure 'Account lockout threshold' is set to '5 or fewer invalid logon attempt(s), but not 0'

Remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy\Account lockout threshold to '5 or fewer invalid logon attempt(s), but not 0'

items.title: Ensure 'Allow Administrator account lockout' is set to 'Enabled'
items.remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policies\Allow Administrator account lockout to 'Enabled'
items.reason: Enabling account lockout policies for the built-in Administrator account will reduce the likelihood of a successful brute force attack.

items.title: Ensure 'Reset account lockout counter after' is set to '15 or more minute(s)'
items.remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy\Reset account lockout counter after to '15 or more minute(s)'
items.reason: If the account lockout policy is left at its default setting or configured with an excessively long interval, the environment may be vulnerable to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. A threat actor could repeatedly attempt to login across multiple accounts, triggering lockouts and disrupting access. Without a defined lockout threshold, administrators would need to manually reset affected accounts. However, by setting a reasonable lockout duration, accounts will automatically unlock after a specified period, reducing administrative overhead and maintaining security.
guidance: Check the configuration source: (net accounts | Select-String 'Lockout observation window' | Out-String) -replace '[^0-9]',''
Expected value: 15

Reason: If the account lockout policy is left at its default setting or configured with an excessively long interval, the environment may be vulnerable to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. A threat actor could repeatedly attempt to login across multiple accounts, triggering lockouts and disrupting access. Without a defined lockout threshold, administrators would need to manually reset affected accounts. However, by setting a reasonable lockout duration, accounts will automatically unlock after a specified period, reducing administrative overhead and maintaining security.
Rule: Ensure 'Reset account lockout counter after' is set to '15 or more minute(s)'
Remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy\Reset account lockout counter after to '15 or more minute(s)'

items.title: Ensure 'Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers' is set to 'Enabled'
items.remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers to 'Enabled'
items.reason: It may be appropriate in some organizations to allow users to install printer drivers on their own workstations. However, in a high security environment, only Administrators should be allowed, not users, to do this, because printer driver installation may unintentionally cause the computer to become less stable. A threat actor could install inappropriate printer drivers in a deliberate attempt to damage the computer, or a user might accidentally install malicious software that masquerades as a printer driver. It is feasible for a threat actor to disguise a Trojan horse program as a printer driver. The program may appear to users as if they must use it to print, but such a program could unleash malicious code on the network.
guidance: Check the configuration source: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Providers\LanMan Print Services\Servers:AddPrinterDrivers
Expected value: 1

Reason: It may be appropriate in some organizations to allow users to install printer drivers on their own workstations. However, in a high security environment, only Administrators should be allowed, not users, to do this, because printer driver installation may unintentionally cause the computer to become less stable. A threat actor could install inappropriate printer drivers in a deliberate attempt to damage the computer, or a user might accidentally install malicious software that masquerades as a printer driver. It is feasible for a threat actor to disguise a Trojan horse program as a printer driver. The program may appear to users as if they must use it to print, but such a program could unleash malicious code on the network.
Rule: Ensure 'Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers' is set to 'Enabled'
Remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers to 'Enabled'

items.title: Ensure 'Microsoft network client: Send unencrypted password to third-party SMB servers' is set to 'Disabled'

These other computers may not use any of the SMB security mechanisms that are included with Windows Server 2003.

Reason: Disabling this setting keeps the cached data independent for each session, both reducing the chance of problems from shared cached data between sessions, and keeping possibly sensitive data separate to each user session.
Rule: Ensure 'Do not use temporary folders per session' is set to 'Disabled'

Remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Remote Desktop Services\Remote Desktop Session Host\Temporary Folders\Do not use temporary folders per session to 'Disabled'
